title: Chair Movement: Calm & Steady
type: Seated mobility / gentle flow; not a medical rehabilitation plan or formal Tai Chi qualification
intro: Move slowly in a comfortable range. If you have a medical condition, recent injury, changing nerve symptoms, dizziness or balance concerns, ask a qualified health professional which movements suit you. Stop for chest pain, faintness, marked breathlessness or new/worsening neurological symptoms.
chair: Choose a strong, stable, non-wheeled chair on a secure floor. Sit with feet supported. Choose a chair and assistance appropriate to your needs; never risk losing balance to meet a posture ideal.
disclaimer: General information only. No weight-loss, body-shape, disease-treatment or individual outcome promise.

sources.name: NHS activity guidelines for older adults

exercises.title: Soft hand glides
exercises.intro: Sit tall but relaxed. Let both hands drift softly forwards and back at a low, comfortable height.
exercises.cue: Move smoothly with natural breathing, without lifting the shoulders.
exercises.easier: Move only the fingers and wrists, or one arm at a time.
exercises.caution: Avoid lifting an arm above a comfortable height. Skip if shoulder pain increases.

exercises.title: Easy shoulder rolls
exercises.intro: Let your arms rest at your sides. Slowly draw small comfortable circles with your shoulders.
exercises.cue: Keep the circles small and unhurried.
exercises.easier: Try a tiny shoulder-blade movement without shrugging.
exercises.caution: Skip with new or increasing shoulder, neck or arm symptoms.

exercises.title: Wrist circles
exercises.intro: Keep elbows close to your body. Gently circle your hands one way, then the other.
exercises.easier: Open and close the fingers instead.

exercises.title: Gentle chest opening
exercises.source: NHS chest stretch; original simplified wording
exercises.intro: Sit upright and let your shoulder blades ease slightly back, without forcing the arms behind you.
exercises.easier: Keep your hands on your thighs and imagine your breastbone lifting very slightly.
exercises.caution: Do not arch the lower back or force painful shoulders.

exercises.title: Seated hip marching
exercises.intro: Sit supported. Gently lift one knee a little, return the foot to the ground, then alternate.
exercises.cue: Lower each foot in control, only as high as feels easy.
exercises.easier: Lift the heel a little rather than the whole foot.
exercises.caution: Stop if leg weakness, pain or radiating symptoms increase.

exercises.title: Ankle points and flexes
exercises.source: NHS ankle stretch / BHF ankle points
exercises.intro: With your foot slightly raised if comfortable, move the toes gently away and then towards you.
exercises.cue: Alternate feet and avoid holding your breath.
exercises.easier: Keep the heel on the floor and gently lift the toes.
exercises.caution: Use a comfortable range, especially with swelling or foot pain.

exercises.title: Optional small neck turns
exercises.source: NHS neck rotation / BHF head turn
exercises.intro: Keep the shoulders relaxed and look a little left, centre, then a little right.
exercises.cue: Small movements. No rolling the head backwards.
exercises.easier: Keep the head centred and look side to side with your eyes.
exercises.caution: Skip with dizziness, new headache, nerve symptoms or neck pain.

exercises.title: Floating hands flow
exercises.intro: Float one hand forwards while the other returns towards your lap. Alternate slowly.
exercises.cue: Relax your shoulders and keep hands below a comfortable height.
exercises.easier: Use just one hand or only your wrists.
exercises.caution: This is a gentle movement cue, not a clinical or traditional Tai Chi lesson.

exercises.title: Optional tiny upper-back turn
exercises.source: NHS upper-body twist; intentionally reduced range
exercises.intro: If a clinician has said turning is suitable, rotate your upper body only a few degrees left and right.
exercises.cue: Keep the movement slight, controlled and comfortable.
exercises.easier: Skip this and repeat soft hand glides.
exercises.caution: Skip with disc-related symptoms, radiating pain, spinal restrictions or uncertain suitability.
